content.text:
The clean options are:

1. Delete `strategy.createCommit` and call `checkpoint.CreateCommit` directly from the tests.
`strategy.createCommit` in [common.go](/home/coder/git/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:1443) is a duplicate of [checkpoint.CreateCommit](/home/coder/git/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/committed.go:1642), and its only call sites are strategy tests like [manual_commit_test.go](/home/coder/git/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_test.go:139) and [clean_test.go](/home/coder/git/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/clean_test.go:76). Since `strategy` already imports `checkpoint`, this is the simplest true consolidation and removes the extra wrapper entirely.

2. Keep `strategy.createCommit`, but make it a one-line delegate to `checkpoint.CreateCommit`.
This is the lowest-risk mechanical change if you want to avoid touching many test call sites:
```go
func createCommit(...) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
    return checkpoint.CreateCommit(ctx, repo, treeHash, parentHash, message, authorName, authorEmail)
}
```
That still centralizes the signing and commit construction logic in one place, matching what `(*checkpoint.GitStore).createCommit` already does in [temporary.go](/home/coder/git/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/temporary.go:793).

3. Extract a lower-level shared helper and have both packages call that.
For example, a helper that builds/encodes/stores the commit object, with `checkpoint.CreateCommit` and any other caller delegating to it. This only makes sense if you expect multiple non-checkpoint packages to need commit creation semantics that are intentionally shared. Right now it looks unnecessary, because `checkpoint.CreateCommit` is already the shared API.

Recommendation: option 1 if you want the codebase cleanest; option 2 if you want the smallest patch. I would not add a new helper package here unless there is a second real production caller with different needs.
I’m removing the strategy-local helper and switching its test call sites to `checkpoint.CreateCommit`, then I’ll run the strategy tests that exercise those paths.
I’ve verified the helper is only referenced from two strategy test files. I’m updating those tests and removing the dead helper from `common.go` now.
